To prepare a corpus for a reliable NovaLearn deployment, a customer must complete the corpus cataloging and audit process defined in Phase 2 of the onboarding playbook [NL-005#NL-005-S04]. This involves the following sequential steps:

1.  **Document Source Audit:** Identify where the company’s knowledge is stored (e.g., SharePoint, Google Drive, local servers, Confluence), catalog the file formats, and document the volume of files in each repository [NL-005#NL-005-S04].
2.  **Format Inspection:** Check that all documents are in supported formats (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, HTML, Markdown, CSV, XLSX). Flag any legacy formats or unsupported file types for conversion [NL-005#NL-005-S04].
3.  **OCR Identification:** Scan the corpus to identify image-only or scanned PDFs. Flag these files for OCR processing, and be aware that they may extend the onboarding timeline due to processing latency [NL-005#NL-005-S04] [NL-009#NL-009-S05].
4.  **Document Taxonomy Definition:** Design the tagging system in KnowledgeHub (e.g., by department, product, region) to enable precise filtering and retrieval, and set up the custom metadata schemas [NL-005#NL-005-S04].
5.  **Corpus Audit Checklist Verification:** Before delivering the Corpus Inventory Sheet, content owners must verify that: all file names are descriptive and exclude special symbols; no duplicate copies of policy manuals exist; scanned files are separated and marked "OCR Required: True"; every document has an assigned department and owner; and source files contain clear heading structures (H1, H2, H3) [NL-005#NL-005-S04].

For overall deployment reliability, Phase 1 (uploading initial policy documentation and establishing folder directory tree structure and taxonomies in KnowledgeHub) should be coordinated with this corpus preparation [NL-028#NL-028-S01] [NL-005#NL-005-S01].
